chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who proposes to another man for his daughter with a specified dowry (mahr), but the father brings her to him with a different one. He said: 'She is married off to him with another dowry specified by her father, and the first dowry belongs to the one with whom he consummated the marriage.'

key_terms.تُزَفُّ: She is married off / escorted to the husband
key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her
key_terms.مَهْر: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What happens to the dowry if the father substitutes a different amount than what was agreed upon during the proposal?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal mechanism of *tadlis* (concealment) in marriage contracts, specifically when the father substitutes the agreed dowry. It establishes that the bride receives the substituted amount as her immediate dowry, while the originally stipulated sum becomes the husband's obligation upon consummation, ensuring financial clarity in marital agreements.
